statement: A food truck's daily profit $P$, in dollars, from selling $n$ tacos is modeled by the equation $P = 3.25n - 140$. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number $140$ in this model?

choices.text: The truck must sell $140$ tacos to break even.
choices.misconception: I thought the number subtracted in the model was the number of tacos needed to cover costs, but breaking even means $3.25n = 140$, which is about $43$ tacos.

choices.text: The truck's profit increases by $\$140$ for each additional taco sold.
choices.misconception: I mixed up the constant term with the rate of change. The change in profit for each extra taco is the coefficient $3.25$, not $140$.

choices.text: The most profit the truck can make in one day is $\$140$.
choices.misconception: I thought the constant set a limit on the profit, but in this model profit keeps growing as $n$ increases, so there is no maximum.

choices.text: The truck has $\$140$ in daily costs that do not depend on how many tacos it sells.

hints: The coefficient of $n$ is the change in profit per taco. The constant tells you what happens when no tacos are sold.
When $n = 0$, $P = -140$: the truck loses $\$140$ even on a day it sells nothing.

solutions.reliable: When $n = 0$, the model gives $P = 3.25(0) - 140 = -140$, so on a day with no sales the truck loses $\$140$. That is the part of the daily cost that does not depend on the number of tacos sold, such as fuel or a parking permit. The $3.25$ is the profit from each taco.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
